system_summary: This legacy relational database (SQLite) acts as a basic Electronic Health Record (EHR) system. It stores patient demographics, administrative encounter headers, clinical diagnosis details, and local reference lookup codes.

entities.name: PT_MSTR
entities.meaning: Patient Master table storing core demographic and contact details.

entities.name: ENC_HDR
entities.meaning: Encounter Header table recording patient visits and admission/discharge dates.

entities.name: DX_DTL
entities.meaning: Diagnosis Details table linking clinical conditions and ICD-10 codes to encounters.

entities.name: REF_CD
entities.meaning: Reference Code lookup table defining internal codes for sex, encounter type, and statuses.

fields.name: DX_DTL.DX_SEQ
fields.meaning: Primary key sequence for diagnosis details

patient_identifier.description: Unique patient identifier used across patient, encounter, and diagnosis tables acting as the primary key/MRN.

integration_pattern.reason: Direct SQLite relational database integration where incremental data extraction can be performed by polling modified records via PT_MSTR.REC_UPD_TS.

data_quality_notes: ICD-10 codes in DX_DTL.DX_CD lack standard decimal dot notation (e.g., 'E119' instead of 'E11.9') and require reformatting for standard terminology servers.
Dates (PT_BIRTH_DT, ADM_DT, DSCH_DT, DX_DT) are stored as 8-digit strings (YYYYMMDD) without time or timezone components.
Sex, encounter types, and status fields rely on internal codes requiring ConceptMap translation using REF_CD lookup data to map to FHIR code systems.
ENC_HDR and DX_DTL lack explicit updated timestamp fields, complicating change data capture for non-patient records.
risks: Concurrency issues and file-locking risks associated with direct database polling against an active SQLite file.
Missing time components on admission/discharge dates can lead to inaccurate encounter duration calculations in FHIR.
Lack of updated timestamps on Encounter and Diagnosis tables risks missed updates unless full tables are regularly scanned.
